drafting_notes:
AUDIENCE: Year 1 (ages 6-7). Frames 6-12 words, everyday home and school scenes, simple vocabulary, spoken in the present: first person and present-anchored main clauses work best, because these words all point from TODAY.
TENSE LAW: tense may PRUNE candidates but never PICK the answer. In every frame at least TWO of the five must stay grammatically possible, and a scene fact must make the final choice. A frame where four words die on tense alone is broken.
ANCHORS come from outside the set: 'this morning', 'before bed', 'after one more sleep', 'at breakfast', 'still' plus visible evidence. Per word: yesterday = aftermath still visible from the finished day ('legs still sore from the race'); today = evidence spanning this same day ('the painting from art class is still wet'); now = this-second urgency mid-action ('the bus doors are closing'); tonight = the dark end of this same day, still ahead ('once it gets dark', after-dinner plans); tomorrow = after a sleep, packing and preparing.
SECOND-FIT TRAPS: now vs today (day-scale evidence for today, second-scale for now); tonight vs tomorrow (tonight belongs to THIS day's darkness); yesterday vs today (yesterday needs finished-before-this-day-began evidence).
SLOTS: place the blank at the start or end of the sentence, where all five deictic adverbs scan naturally.
SURFACES: these are adverbs; the surface form of every candidate is the word itself, unchanged, in every frame.

contrasts.line: Yesterday is finished before this morning. Today is the whole day we are in.
Yesterday is already over. Now is this exact second.
Yesterday happened before this morning. Tonight is still ahead after dark.
Yesterday is before this day began. Tomorrow comes after a sleep.
Today is the day we are in. Yesterday was already over before this morning.
Today can stretch from morning to hometime. Now is only this exact second.
Today is the whole day we are in. Tonight is only the dark part still ahead.
Today is before the next sleep. Tomorrow is after that sleep.
Now is this exact second. Yesterday is already over.
Now means right this second. Today can mean any time in this day.
Now is happening right away. Tonight waits until it gets dark.
Now is right this second. Tomorrow is after a sleep.
Tonight is after dark on this same day. Yesterday is already over.
Tonight is the dark part still ahead. Today is the whole day we are in.
Tonight waits until after dark. Now is this exact second.
Tonight comes before this sleep. Tomorrow comes after a sleep.
Tomorrow comes after a sleep. Yesterday was before this day began.
Tomorrow is after a sleep. Today is the day we are in.
Tomorrow is after a sleep. Now is this exact second.
Tomorrow comes after a sleep. Tonight is the dark part before that sleep.
